routes.label: Cancel the positive shrinking height factor before taking the limit
Cancel the common height and compare the chord lengths

question:
In this diagram the center of the circle is \(O,\) the radius is \(a\) inches, chord \(EF\) is parallel to chord \(CD,\) \(O,\) \(G,\) \(H,\) \(J\) are collinear, and \(G\) is the midpoint of \(CD.\) Let \(K\) (square inches) represent the area of trapezoid \(CDFE\) and let \(R\) (square inches) represent the area of rectangle \(ELMF.\) Then, as \(CD\) and \(EF\) are translated upward so that \(OG\) increases toward the value \(a,\) while \(JH\) always equals \(HG,\) the ratio \(K:R\) becomes arbitrarily close to:

[Figure 1](figures/1968_AMC_12_Q35_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The trapezoid and rectangle have the same height \(HG\). Canceling this height first lets us compare their areas even as both regions shrink.

The figure places \(J\) on the circle above \(O\), with \(H\) between \(G\) and \(J\). Let \(h=HG=HJ\). For positions near the top, \(0<h<a/2\), and
\[
JG=2h,\qquad OG=a-2h,\qquad OH=a-h.
\]
Because \(G\) is the midpoint of chord \(CD\), the line \(OG\) is perpendicular to \(CD\). It is also perpendicular to the parallel chord \(EF\), so \(H\) is the midpoint of \(EF\).

A radius to a chord endpoint, the perpendicular distance from the center, and half the chord form a right triangle. Applying Pythagoras to the two chords gives
\[
\left(\frac{CD}{2}\right)^2
=a^2-(a-2h)^2=4h(a-h),
\]
\[
\left(\frac{EF}{2}\right)^2
=a^2-(a-h)^2=h(2a-h).
\]
The trapezoid has bases \(CD\) and \(EF\), while the rectangle has width \(EF\). Both have height \(h\), so
\[
\frac KR
=\frac{(CD+EF)h/2}{EF\,h}
=\frac12+\frac{CD}{2EF}.
\]
All the lengths being canceled are positive. Using the chord-square expressions and taking positive square roots now gives
\[
\frac KR=\frac12+\sqrt{\frac{a-h}{2a-h}}.
\]
As \(OG\) increases toward \(a\), the length \(h\) decreases toward zero. Since \(a>0\), the denominator inside the square root approaches the positive number \(2a\). Consequently,
\[
\frac KR\longrightarrow
\frac12+\sqrt{\frac{a}{2a}}
=\boxed{\frac12+\frac1{\sqrt2}}.
\]
At the endpoint both areas are zero; the calculation uses the ratio at positive heights approaching that endpoint. The answer is choice \(\boxed{D}\).
